newsitem.title: USA: GM invests $300 million in Michigan stamping plant.
newsitem.headline: GM invests $300 million in Michigan stamping plant.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Monday it will invest about $300 million at the Flint Metal Centre for new manufacturing equipment and tooling to prepare the plant for future product programmes.

GM also said it will update existing presses at the metal stamping plant, which is a part of its Metal Fabricating Division. The facility produces engine cradles and major and minor sheet metal panels for GM cars, trucks and mid-size vans.
The automaker in 1994 initiated an aggressive programme to simplify its stamping operations and use common manufacturing equipment and processes throughout its 13 North American stamping plants.

GM said its investments in the Flint Metal Centre will help accelerate its plan to identify common processes or best practices that can be shared with other facilities. It said the new equipment will enhance the facility's ability to respond quickly to changes in product mix or customer preference demands.
The plant employs 3,996 people, or nearly 12 percent of the Metal Fabricating Division's 34,000-member work force.
GM's stock was unchanged at $57 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
